title: Microsegmented pricing & headcount phasing playbook (Q2 2027)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores microsegmented pricing moves across product tiers (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and ties each scenario to a headcount phasing plan for FY27 Q2–Q4. The goal is to produce a small set of executable levers that materially change 12‑month ARR and unit economics while keeping hiring aligned to delivery risk. This is intentionally a working model: assumptions are highlighted and marked for validation with go-to-market and product teams.

Key questions this doc answers (working):
- If we implement a 3‑tier microsegmented price list (Core / Pro / Enterprise) with targeted elasticity by segment, what is the expected ARR delta at 6 and 12 months?
- Which hiring (sales/solutions/eng) must accelerate to capture demand, and which hires can be deferred without losing funnel?
- Sensitivity to token price moves for Hosted API (per-1k-token price) and committed capacity discounts for Dedicated.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Run a controlled pilot of microsegmented pricing for 8 weeks across new accounts only (US + EU) with: Core = base price, Pro = +30% price with controlled feature gating (higher SLA, dedicated model variants), Enterprise = custom pricing (negotiated).
- Hold back 30% of planned Q2 field hires in Solutions (deferred 2 quarters) to preserve runway; reallocate 50% of the recruiting budget into AE acceleration for Enterprise pilot accounts.
- Execute 3 sensitivity buckets (see scenarios) in the first 8 weeks with automated telemetry to measure conversion drop-off and average tokens/seat.

Assumptions (high level):
- Time window: Modeling immediate 12 months following Q2 2027 change.
- Baseline ARR (today): $72.4M. Baseline mix: Hosted API 60% ARR, Dedicated 30% ARR, Private 10% ARR.
- Avg revenue per active account by tier: Hosted base account = $2.4k/mo, Dedicated base = $45k/mo, Private base = $120k/mo (large enterprise).
- Token economics (Hosted): base price = $0.0005 per 1k tokens (note: tokens in thousands), marginal cost per 1k tokens = $0.00012 after batching/caching.
- Elasticity assumptions derived from historical small price tests + competitor signals (conservative): Hosted price elasticity by segment = Core: -0.5, Pro: -0.8, Enterprise: -0.2 (enterprise largely inelastic).
- Capacity discounts for Dedicated: Standard commit discount = 30% off hosted list; increasing commit to 40% accelerates conversions in medium-sized customers but increases unit cost via reserved capacity commitments.
- Hiring cost assumptions: fully loaded AE = $220k/year, Solutions engineer = $190k/year, Infra/ops engineer = $240k/year. Hiring lead time = 8–12 weeks nominal.

Scenario definitions (tested in model):
- Base (no pricing change): baseline ARR growth = 10% YoY, hiring plan = nominal (as proposed in Q1 hiring slate).
- Upsell-Premium (pro strategy): introduce Pro tier +30% list vs base for higher SLA/features; expect 8% of Hosted customers to upgrade within 6 months, hosted elasticity applied to net new signups only.
- Price-Discount (volume play): lower Hosted tier by 15% to drive volume; assume elasticity = -1.6 for low-end startups (aggressive), net new acquisition increase of +25% in Hosted active accounts within 4 months.
- Enterprise-Focus: price stability on Hosted but reprice Dedicated to encourage commits (5–10% lower for larger commits) and invest in AE hiring to push Enterprise deals.

Interpretation notes (working):
- Enterprise-Focus yields the largest ARR upside and margin expansion but requires earlier hiring and a larger committed capacity build (capex + infra) to service increased Dedicated demand. The hiring/salary profile also frontloads costs which increases short term cash burn.
- Upsell-Premium captures high-margin expansion inside existing customers with minimal infra changes. This is the least operationally disruptive and has good margin leverage.
- Price-Discount increases acquisition but compresses margin; it is only attractive if CAC drops substantially or if it brings enough high-usage accounts that convert to higher tiers.

Key sensitivity knobs to instrument in the pilot:
1) Conversion delta to Pro from Core (weekly measurement per cohort).
2) Average tokens per account post-upgrade (tokens drive marginal costs).
3) Dedicated commit uptake elasticity by seat and vertical (measure pipeline conversion by cohort).
4) CAC and time-to-first-purchase by pricing cohort.

Telemetry & acceptance criteria for pilot (8 weeks):
- Primary metric: incremental monthly recurring revenue from pilot cohort >= 12% above modeled expectation for Upsell-Premium in week 8.
- Secondary metrics: churn delta < 1% absolute, average tokens/account change < 10% (unless expected), Net Revenue Retention improvement >= 4% within 3 months.
- Hiring gate: do not commit to >60% of planned AE hires until pilot passes acceptance at week 8.

Operational notes for finance/infrastructure alignment:
- If Enterprise-Focus is chosen, we must prebook an additional 15 x A100-style GPU capacity in Q3 to support forecasted Dedicated growth. Finance: model cashflow for that purchase as either CapEx (on-prem style) or commit to cloud reserved instances (op-ex with minimum 12 month commit).
- Accounting: treat upgrade revenues as ARR with deferred revenue recognition as per current policy; ensure discounts for Dedicated commits are tracked by contract id for audit.

Action items (next 30 days):
- Finance: finalize sensitivity model inputs with GTM (Asha, Diego) and freeze elasticities used in pilot (owner: Asha). Target: Jan 31.
- GTM: identify 150 pilot accounts across US/EU for A/B test; prioritize existing mid-market Hosted accounts with signals of high token usage (owner: Maya). Target: Feb 7.
- Product: implement feature gating for Pro tier and telemetry hooks (owner: Jonah). Target: Feb 14.
- Ops: provide capacity cushion options for Dedicated (owner: Infra-Eng lead). Target: Feb 14.

Open questions / validation points (notes to self):
- Need better granularity on Hosted token cost by sequence length distribution (short context heavy vs long streaming). Current marginal cost estimate is coarse.
- CAC sensitivity by cohort for the pricing discount play — we lack recent A/B experiments at >10% price moves.
- Legal: confirm contract terms and how pricing tiers map to refund/SLAs for pilot.

Appendix: quick model outputs (single-line exports)
- Baseline ARR: $72,400,000
- Upsell-Premium 12m ARR: $80,000,000 (approx +10.5%)
- Enterprise-Focus 12m ARR: $81,700,000 (approx +12.8%)
- Projected incremental hiring cost if Enterprise-Focus chosen (first 6 months): ~$2.4M additional fully-loaded

Notes on provenance and model caveats:
- Elasticities are a mix of historical internal small tests (2025), third-party market signals, and conservative judgment. Treat as hypothesis.
- Model does not attempt to forecast macroeconomic demand shock. Add sensitivity if we see >5% QoQ change in API token growth.
